extracted.intended_audience: low-income inventors and small businesses seeking pro bono patent assistance in Virginia, West Virginia, or DC (and volunteer patent attorneys in those jurisdictions)
extracted.subtask_description: Eligibility and application requirements for the FCBA Regional Patent Pro Bono Program’s Inventor Assistance Program (IAP), covering required training/certification, financial-eligibility thresholds, invention-description standards, and regional residency constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding of the patent process (training/certificate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Inventors must show that they understand the patent process and what they can do with a patent once received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This can be done by successfully completing a USPTO training module found on the pro se/pro bono page of the USPTO website. A certificate of completion is available from that training module. Applicants will be required to provide that certificate to the FCBA IAP before their application for pro bono assistance will be processed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial eligibility (income threshold)
rubrics_metrics.description: All applicants must provide financial information so a determination can be made that they qualify for the program; generally the FCBA IAP uses an income threshold of 300% of the Federal poverty guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To determine qualification, the IAP will take into account the number of dependents in the inventor’s household and multiply the poverty guideline number for that household size by three. If the inventor’s income is less than 300% of the Federal poverty guidelines, then the inventor is financially eligible for participation in the regional program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to describe the invention (enablement requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor must be able to describe his invention: not simply having an idea for an invention, but able to explain how someone could make the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement distinguishes a concrete, describable invention from a mere idea and is used to assess whether the inventor can be assisted and matched with a volunteer attorney.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional/jurisdictional eligibility (residency requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must live within Virginia, West Virginia, or DC to apply to the regional FCBA IAP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an inventor is not within one of these jurisdictions, the USPTO’s pro bono website provides information about which regional programs cover each state. Applicants in-region should fill out the Application form (note: the form may not appear properly if connected to a VPN).
